prompt: Who creates the planner's `MainActivity` object when somebody taps the icon?
hint: You write the class and never call its constructor.

choices.text: The system, after reading the manifest
choices.why: Right: Android finds the `LAUNCHER` activity in the manifest, makes the instance and then calls its callbacks.

choices.text: `setContent`, the first time it runs
choices.why: `setContent` runs inside `onCreate`, on an activity that already exists.

choices.text: Your `Application` class, by calling `MainActivity()`
choices.why: An activity made with its constructor in your code has no window and no lifecycle.

choices.text: The launcher app, which loads the class into its own process
choices.why: The launcher only asks; the activity lives in the planner's own process.

prompt: Why does the lesson's `onPause` log BEFORE calling `super.onPause()`, while `onResume` logs after?
hint: Think of the order the lines appear in.

choices.text: The framework throws if a log comes after `super` in a callback going down
choices.why: The framework only requires that `super` is called, not where.

choices.text: So the log reads in the order things happen to the activity
choices.why: Right: going up, the framework does its part first; going down, your part is the last thing before the framework's.

choices.text: `Log.d` does not work after `super.onPause()` has returned
choices.why: Logging works at any point; `onStop` and `onDestroy` log the same way.

choices.text: It is a style rule for Kotlin, unrelated to Android
choices.why: Kotlin has no such rule; the order is about reading the log.

prompt: A Compose app's activity extends `ComponentActivity` and not `AppCompatActivity`. What would `AppCompatActivity` add?
hint: It came before Compose.

choices.text: The `setContent` function itself
choices.why: `setContent` comes from `androidx.activity` and works on `ComponentActivity`.

choices.text: The lifecycle callbacks
choices.why: Every activity has them; they come from Android's own `Activity`.

choices.text: The toolbar and theming of the pre-Compose view system
choices.why: Right: it builds on the same class and adds the old views' toolbar and themes, which a Compose app does not use.

choices.text: Support for running on Android 8
choices.why: `minSdk = 26` is Android 8 already, with `ComponentActivity`.

prompt: The test launches the activity and then sends it Home. Put the callbacks in the order the log printed them.
hint: Up three steps, then down two.

prompt: Match each pair of callbacks to the question whose answer it brackets.
hint: Outer, middle, inner.

pairs.right: Is it the one in front, taking touches?

prompt: The user presses Home and comes back a minute later. Which callback does NOT run on the way back?
hint: Is it the same object?

choices.text: `onStart`
choices.why: It runs: the activity becomes visible again.

choices.text: `onCreate`
choices.why: Right: the instance survived, so it is not created again.

choices.text: `onResume`
choices.why: It runs: the activity comes back in front.

prompt: In the test's log, Home produced `onPause` and `onStop` and no `onSaveInstanceState`. What does the lesson conclude?
hint: A test drives the transitions; it is not the system.

choices.text: That Home never saves state, so the `Bundle` is only for rotation
choices.why: On a device the system calls it after `onStop`; that is what process death relies on.

choices.text: That `moveToState` does not simulate that call, which a device does make
choices.why: Right: Google documents the call after `onStop` since Android 9; the rotation test shows it.

choices.text: That the activity was finished instead of stopped
choices.why: `onDestroy` did not run after Home, so nothing was finished.

choices.text: That Robolectric needs `GraphicsMode.NATIVE` for the call
choices.why: Graphics mode is about drawing pixels, not lifecycle calls.

prompt: After Back, `onDestroy` logged `finishing ___`.
hint: The user said they were done with this screen.

prompt: What does the system do to the activity when the phone is turned, by default?
hint: Count the instances in the log.

choices.text: Destroys it and creates a new instance
choices.why: Right: the log showed `instance 2` with `saved state: true`.

choices.text: Keeps it and calls `onConfigurationChanged`
choices.why: Only if the manifest opts out with `android:configChanges`, which the course avoids.

choices.text: Pauses it and redraws only the composables
choices.why: The whole activity goes, from `onPause` to `onDestroy`.

choices.text: Kills the process and starts the app again from the launcher
choices.why: The process stayed: `ProcessWide.created` reached 2 in the same process.

prompt: After one rotation, what number did `ProcessWide.created` print in the new `onCreate`?
hint: `instance … in this process`.

prompt: A form keeps the name being typed in `private var draft = ""` on the activity. The user turns the phone. What is in `draft` afterwards?
hint: Whose field is it?

choices.text: What was typed, since the process survived
choices.why: The process survived and the object did not; the field belonged to the object.

choices.text: An empty string, in a new instance
choices.why: Right: a field of the activity goes with the instance that was destroyed.

choices.text: What was typed, because `onSaveInstanceState` saves every field
choices.why: It saves what the code or the framework puts in the `Bundle`, and a plain field is neither.

choices.text: `null`, because Kotlin resets it
choices.why: The new instance runs the initialiser again, which gives `""`.

prompt: A colleague adds `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize"` to stop the form emptying on rotation. What still empties it?
hint: Only the changes listed are handled.

choices.text: Nothing: the attribute covers every configuration change
choices.why: It covers the two it names.

choices.text: Turning the phone back the other way
choices.why: Both directions are an orientation change, and both are now handled.

choices.text: Switching the phone to dark mode
choices.why: Right: dark mode is not in the list, so the activity is still rebuilt and the field lost.

choices.text: Calling `onConfigurationChanged` from the form
choices.why: The system calls it; it rebuilds nothing.

prompt: The system kills the planner's process in the background to free memory. Which callback runs first?
hint: Step 2 of the sequence.

choices.text: `onDestroy`, with `finishing false`
choices.why: Nothing runs: a killed process has no chance to call anything.

choices.text: `onSaveInstanceState`
choices.why: It ran earlier, when the activity stopped; the kill itself runs nothing.

choices.text: None at all
choices.why: Right: the process is gone with every object in it, which is why state is saved at `onStop`.

choices.text: `onPause`, then `onStop`
choices.why: Those ran when the user left; the kill comes later.

prompt: After process death the user reopens the planner from the recent apps. What does `onCreate` log?
hint: A new process, an old `Bundle`.

choices.text: `instance 1 in this process, saved state: true`
choices.why: Right: the counter starts again in a new process, and the saved `Bundle` is handed over.

choices.text: `instance 2 in this process, saved state: true`
choices.why: That is rotation, where the process survives; here `ProcessWide` was lost with the process.

choices.text: `instance 1 in this process, saved state: false`
choices.why: That is a fresh start; the system kept the `Bundle` to restore the screen.

choices.text: Nothing: the app opens on the launcher's home screen
choices.why: The task remembered the activity, and the system recreates it.

prompt: Match each place a value lives to the first event in the table that loses it.
hint: Columns, left to right: rotation, Home, process death, swipe away.

pairs.right: the user swiping the app away

prompt: Under how many kilobytes does Google's documentation recommend keeping saved state?
hint: Past that, a transaction can throw `TransactionTooLargeException`.

prompt: Why does an Android app start in a fraction of a second although the framework is large?
hint: The first process the system keeps from boot.

choices.text: The framework is compiled into each APK
choices.why: No APK carries the framework; lesson 1's dex was libraries.

choices.text: Its process is a fork of the zygote, which has the framework loaded
choices.why: Right: the copy starts with the classes already in memory.

choices.text: The previous process is reused for every app
choices.why: Each app gets its own process; it is a copy of the zygote, not a reuse.

choices.text: The launcher keeps the app running in the background
choices.why: The launcher only asks; the speed comes from `fork`.

prompt: The window test listed the views inside `android.R.id.content`. What did it find?
hint: `views in the content`.

choices.text: One view per composable on the screen
choices.why: Composables are not views; Compose draws them inside one.

choices.text: A `TextView` with the sentence
choices.why: `Text` is a composable, drawn by Compose, not a `TextView`.

choices.text: One `ComposeView`
choices.why: Right: `setContent` makes one `ComposeView` the activity's content.

choices.text: No view at all, since Compose replaces the window
choices.why: Compose keeps the window and the activity, and puts its one view in the content frame.

prompt: Why did the test run with `recordRoborazziDebug` rather than `testDebugUnitTest` to get the PNG?
hint: Roborazzi has modes.

choices.text: `testDebugUnitTest` cannot run Robolectric tests
choices.why: It ran the lifecycle tests, which are Robolectric tests.

choices.text: Roborazzi writes a picture only when it is recording
choices.why: Right: in the other modes it compares against one, which lesson 21 shows.

choices.text: The record task gives the screen a size
choices.why: The size comes from `@Config(qualifiers = …)`.

choices.text: Only the record task draws real pixels
choices.why: Pixels come from `@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)`, in either task.

prompt: `@Config(qualifiers = "w320dp-h200dp-xhdpi")` produced a PNG how many pixels wide?
hint: xhdpi is twice the original density.

prompt: In a single-activity Compose app, what is moving from the course list to a course's sessions?
hint: A screen is a function.

choices.text: A new activity, started with an intent
choices.why: That was the old shape, one activity per screen.

choices.text: Another composable, with the course as an ordinary parameter
choices.why: Right: lesson 9 builds the back stack that decides which composable is shown.

choices.text: A `Bundle` passed through `onSaveInstanceState`
choices.why: The `Bundle` is for restoring a screen, not for moving between screens.

choices.text: A second `setContent` call replacing the first
choices.why: `setContent` runs once; the screens change inside the composition it starts.

prompt: An exported activity reads a course id from an intent's extras. Why does the lesson say to check that id like any other input?
hint: Who can send that intent?

choices.text: Extras are lost after process death
choices.why: The question is who wrote the value, not whether it survives.

choices.text: Every app on the phone is allowed to start it, with whatever it puts inside
choices.why: Right: `exported="true"` is a door from outside, so the id comes from a stranger.

choices.text: Kotlin cannot type-check values inside a `Bundle`
choices.why: A wrong type is a nuisance; a hostile value of the right type is the risk.

choices.text: The launcher modifies extras before delivering them
choices.why: The launcher sends no extras; other apps might.

prompt: Which of these survive both a rotation AND process death? Choose all that apply.
hint: The table in section 05.

choices.text: A course id put in the saved `Bundle`
choices.why: Yes: the system keeps the `Bundle` across both.

choices.text: A list in an `object`
choices.why: No: it survives rotation and dies with the process.

choices.text: A session stored in a database
choices.why: Yes: it is on disk.

choices.text: A field of `MainActivity`
choices.why: No: rotation alone loses it.

hint: The old instance goes down; the new one comes up.
items: `onCreate: instance 2 in this process, saved state: true`

prompt: A tester on a phone with lots of memory says the planner always restores the open course. A student on a cheap phone says it opens on an empty screen. Which explanation fits both?
hint: Which phone's system kills background processes more?

choices.text: The open course lives in an `object`, which process death loses
choices.why: Right: on the big phone the process survives; on the small one it is killed, and the `object` with it.

choices.text: The cheap phone runs an older Android without `onSaveInstanceState`
choices.why: Every Android has it; `minSdk` is 26.

choices.text: The student pressed Back instead of Home
choices.why: Possible for one report, but it does not explain why it depends on the phone.

choices.text: Rotation is handled differently on small screens
choices.why: Rotation behaves the same; memory is what differs.
